cards.explanation: The answer is that the word of the LORD is rare. The text says "…the word of the LORD was rare, and visions were scarce." In plain words, hearing from God was not an everyday thing in those days. It was quieter than my bakery when the oven timer finally stops.

The answer is temple, the temple of the LORD. The text puts Samuel lying down there, right where the ark of God was located. That's a pretty special place to be tucked in for the night. I've slept in a junk drawer, friends, so I'm in no position to judge anyone's bedroom.

The answer is True. Samuel runs to Eli and says, "Here I am, for you have called me." That tells us Samuel thinks Eli is the one who called. The text also says Samuel "…did not yet know the LORD…" (1 Samuel 3:7).
The answer is lie down. Eli says, "I did not call… Go back and lie down." Short, simple and sleepy. I think Eli just wants the boy to get some rest.
The answer is False. Samuel doesn't stay put. He got up, went to Eli, and said, "Here I am, for you have called me." Eli answered, "My son, I did not call…" This kid was running laps in the dark.

The answer is that the word of the LORD hasn't been revealed to him. The text says Samuel "…did not yet know the LORD, because the word of the LORD had not yet been revealed to him." Twice he heard his name and ran to Eli, and this is what the text tells us about him right then. The word of the LORD hadn't been revealed to him yet.
The answer is True, and it happens on the third call. The text says, "Then Eli realized that it was the LORD who was calling the boy." It took three rounds, friends, but Eli put it together.
The answer is to ask the LORD to speak because he's listening. Eli says to tell Him, "Speak, LORD, for Your servant is listening." Short and simple. Samuel doesn't need a speech, just open ears.

The answer is that the LORD comes and stands there. The text says, "Then the LORD came and stood there, calling as before, 'Samuel! Samuel!'" This time the LORD Himself comes and stands there. That's the difference on this call.
The answer is Eli. The LORD says, "On that day I will carry out against Eli everything I have spoken about his house, from beginning to end." This is a heavy word. It's about Eli's house.

The answer is that his sons blasphemed God and he did not restrain them. That's what the LORD says: "…his sons blasphemed God and he did not restrain them." It's the iniquity "…of which he knows…" This is a heavy part of the story.

The answer is False, and this one is heavy. The LORD says, "The iniquity of Eli’s house shall never be atoned for by sacrifice or offering." Sacrifice and offering are both named, and neither covers it. It's a sober verse.
The answer is afraid. The text says Samuel "…was afraid to tell Eli the vision…" I think anyone would feel that with a message like this. It's a hard thing to carry to someone you know.
The answer is every word with nothing hidden. Eli says, "Do not hide it from me." He also asks for "…anything He said to you." He wants all of it, friends.

The answer is False. The text says, "…Samuel told him everything and did not hide a thing from him." That's everything, with nothing hidden. Even after being afraid to tell it (1 Samuel 3:15), he told it all.

The answer is that Eli says to let the LORD do what He sees as good. He says, "He is the LORD… Let Him do what is good in His eyes." It's a reply after hard news, and I think it sounds calm. I think that took something.

The answer is that the LORD lets none of them fall to the ground. The text says the LORD "…let none of Samuel’s words fall to the ground." Every word counted. It's a good sign for the boy who kept running to the wrong room.
The answer is prophet. The text says all Israel from Dan to Beersheba knew that Samuel "…was confirmed as a prophet of the LORD." The whole land knew. News traveled that way back then too.

The answer is True. The text says, "…the LORD continued to appear at Shiloh, because there He revealed Himself to Samuel by His word." Back in verse 1, the word was rare. Now it keeps showing up, friends.
